```{r setup}
library(liminal2)
library(arrow)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

## Purpose

This vignette benchmarks how the seven dimension scores and the final
liminality differ across **all models available on the Panama API**, and
presents the evidence in tables. It makes the choice of the default
model (`glm-5.3`) an auditable, visible decision instead of an
assertion.

The benchmark is **evaluation, not calibration**: the scenario ladder is
used as a benchmark metric, never as a fitting target, and the results
are never used to re-tune prompts or anchors. Scores from different
models must not be pooled.

```{r data}
results <- arrow::read_parquet(
  system.file(
    "extdata",
    "model-comparison-results.parquet",
    package = "liminal2"
  )
)

scenarios <- unique(results$scenario)
models <- unique(results$model)
benchmark_date <- unique(results$benchmark_date)
```

The benchmark was regenerated from live API calls on `r benchmark_date`
and covers `r length(models)` models (`r paste(models, collapse = ", ")`
), the six scenarios S1--S6 and the seven dimension prompts, with each
cell run twice to quantify run-to-run stability at temperature 0. The
raw scores, token usage and cost of every call are cached in
`inst/extdata/model-comparison-results.parquet`.

## Liminality per model and scenario

Each row of the headline table aggregates the two repetitions. The
condition scores are computed from the raw scores with the fixed
conversion from the specification (`condition = 1 - raw / 10`) and
aggregated with `measure_liminal_space()`.

```{r liminality}
liminality <- results |>
  group_by(model, scenario, rep) |>
  summarise(
    liminality = liminal2::measure_liminal_space(
      stats::setNames(1 - raw_score / 10, dimension)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r table1}
headline <- liminality |>
  group_by(model, scenario) |>
  summarise(
    mean_liminality = mean(liminality),
    rep_delta = abs(diff(liminality)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scenarios)) |>
  arrange(model, scenario)

ladder <- liminality |>
  mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scenarios)) |>
  arrange(model, rep, scenario) |>
  group_by(model, rep) |>
  summarise(ladder_ok = all(diff(liminality) > 0), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(ladder_ok = all(ladder_ok), .groups = "drop")

stability <- headline |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(mean_delta = mean(rep_delta), .groups = "drop")

cost <- results |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(total_cost = sum(cost, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

table1 <- headline |>
  mutate(mean_liminality = round(mean_liminality, 2)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = mean_liminality) |>
  left_join(stability, by = "model") |>
  left_join(ladder, by = "model") |>
  left_join(cost, by = "model") |>
  mutate(
    mean_delta = round(mean_delta, 2),
    total_cost = round(total_cost, 2)
  )

knitr::kable(table1)
```

`ladder_ok` is `TRUE` when the six liminalities are strictly increasing
along S1--S6 in both repetitions, the invariant the measure must
satisfy. `mean_delta` is the mean absolute difference between the two
repetitions across scenarios: the stability of the model as a scorer.
At temperature 0 it is often small but not necessarily zero, because
batched inference on the serving backend makes even greedy sampling
vary between runs; non-zero values quantify that residual jitter. `total_cost` is summed over all calls of the benchmark.

## Raw dimension scores

The table below shows the mean raw score (0 = small space, 10 = large
space) over the two repetitions for every model, scenario and
dimension, and the absolute difference between the repetitions. This is
where dimension-level disagreements between models become visible.

```{r table2}
table2 <- results |>
  group_by(model, scenario, dimension) |>
  summarise(
    mean_raw = mean(raw_score),
    rep_delta = if (dplyr::n() == 2) {
      abs(diff(raw_score))
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(across(c(mean_raw, rep_delta), ~ round(.x, 1)))

knitr::kable(table2)
```

## Reading the benchmark

```{r findings}
n_ladder_ok <- sum(ladder$ladder_ok)
default_model <- "glm-5.3"
default_liminality <- liminality |>
  filter(model == default_model) |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarise(liminality = mean(liminality), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(factor(scenario, levels = scenarios)) |>
  pull(liminality)
```

`r n_ladder_ok` of `r length(models)` models reproduce the strictly
increasing ladder. The default model, `r default_model`, yields the
liminalities
`r paste(sprintf("%.2f", default_liminality), collapse = " < ")` along
S1--S6. When a model deviates, the raw-score table above shows which
dimensions drive the difference: disagreement concentrated in one
dimension is evidence about that dimension's anchors, while diffuse
disagreement is evidence about the model. Stability deltas above zero
mean the model does not score deterministically even at temperature 0,
and its scores should not be compared at a finer resolution than the
observed jitter. Per the specification, such findings feed the anchor
review; they are never used to re-tune the prompts on these scenarios.

Regenerate the cached results with:

```sh
R CMD INSTALL -l "$(rv library)" .
rv run data-raw/model_comparison.R
```
